record.original_question: A continuous mapping f : B n → Rn , where B n = {x : x ∈ Rn , |x| < 1}, and n ≥ 2, is said to be proper if f −1 (K) is a compact subset of B n whenever K is a proper subset of f (B n ). Let Bf = {z : z ∈ B n , f is not a local homeomorphism at z}. Is it true that, if (i) n ≥ 3, (ii) f : B n → Rn is proper and quasi-analytic, and (iii) Bf is compact then f is necessarily injective? Note that the mapping f (z) = z 2 , where z ∈ B 2 , shows that the conjecture is false when n = 2. The conjecture is known to be true in the special case that f (B n ) = B n , n ≥ 3. The conjecture is a special case of a more general open problem in [773]. (M. Vuorinen)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\geq 3$ and let $B^n=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:|x|<1\}$ denote the open unit ball. A continuous map $f:B^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ is called proper if $f^{-1}(K)$ is a compact subset of $B^n$ for every compact set $K$ contained in $f(B^n)$. Assume in addition that $f$ is quasiregular (i.e., $f$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W^{1,n}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B^n,\mathbb{R}^n)$, is non-constant, and there exists a constant $K\geq 1$ such that $|Df(x)|^n\leq K\, J_f(x)$ for almost every $x\in B^n$, where $J_f$ is the Jacobian determinant). Let
$$B_f=\{z\in B^n:f\text{ is not a local homeomorphism at }z\}$$
denote the branch set of $f$. Suppose that $B_f$ is compact. Must $f$ be injective on $B^n$?

(Note: the planar winding map $f(z)=z^2$ on $B^2$ shows the analogous statement fails when $n=2$; and the case $f(B^n)=B^n$ for $n\geq 3$ is known.)
artifact.status_search_result: Kauranen, Luisto, and Tengvall (arXiv:1904.12645, Bull. London Math. Soc., 2022) prove that a proper branched covering from $B^n$ onto an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with compact branch set is a homeomorphism when $n=3$ or when the branch set is empty, thereby resolving Vuorinen's question in dimension 3. The case $n\geq 4$ appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On proper branched coverings and a question of Vuorinen
status_evidence.snippet: Proper branched coverings defined on the Euclidean n-ball in the case when the branch set is compact are shown to be homeomorphisms when n=3 or when the branch set is empty.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is confirmed for n=3, leaving higher dimensions open.

status_evidence.title: On proper branched coverings and a question of Vuorinen — Bull. London Math. Soc.
status_evidence.snippet: Such mappings are homeomorphisms when n=3 or when the branch set is empty.
status_evidence.claim: Published resolution of the n=3 case of Vuorinen's question.
